subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Pipe Materials and Sizing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pipe Materials and Sizing usable.

hook.text: Steel, copper, PVC — each pipe material has strengths and weak spots.

buildup.text: Steel handles high pressure. Copper resists corrosion. PVC is cheap and light.

discovery.text: Pipe diameter sets velocity. Too narrow means high friction. Too wide wastes money.

twist.text: Corrosion buildup narrows pipes over years, raising friction and cutting flow.

climax.text: Engineers balance pressure rating, cost, life span, and flow when choosing.

punchline.text: The right pipe is the one that lasts and pays for itself.

quiz.question: Why does corrosion inside pipes increase energy costs over time?
options: Corroded pipes leak, losing water that must be replaced
Buildup narrows the bore, raising friction and demanding more pump power
Corrosion weakens the pipe, requiring lower operating pressures
